This restored weekday foot traffic near offices and transit hubs will continue lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks as workers resume lunch and after-work shopping.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -32.3 at t-3w to -13.6 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days relative to the prior 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing its upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility crosses above -35 points (a 5+ point weekly improvement), it signals renewed public transport usage enabling access to retail districts, which should raise RETAIL_REC within two weeks of the crossing.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly mean rises above -35 points, improving at least 5 points from the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -45.6 to -39.9 between t-3w and t-1w before flattening at -40.1
failure_condition: TRANSIT crosses the -35 threshold but RETAIL_REC does not increase in the following two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous recovery in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT reflects a compounding return-to-routine effect: commuters both travel more and work more in-person, jointly amplifying retail footfall beyond what either series predicts alone, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both series show improving trends over the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC growth over the next 4 weeks is no greater than the growth predicted by WORKPLACES or TRANSIT individually, indicating no synergistic effect.

regime_hint: seasonal transition (autumn to winter in Victoria)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 28 days despite continued decline in PARKS mobility.

evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM was 3.6 at t-1w and 2.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining flat, indicating no saturation effect.

evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell from -10.7 at t-1w to -13.7 at t-0w
